stories.title: Zambia's president Hichilema wins re-election with big economic promises
stories.summary: Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema won a second term on Tuesday after campaigning on his record of economic recovery, including a major debt restructuring deal. The 64-year-old faces pressure to deliver more jobs and opportunities as critics accuse his government of failing to ease poverty and becoming less tolerant of dissent.
stories.headline: Zambia's president Hichilema wins re-election with big economic promises

opening: Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema won a second term on Tuesday after campaigning on his record of economic recovery, including a major debt restructuring deal.
The 64-year-old faces pressure to deliver more jobs and opportunities as critics accuse his government of failing to ease poverty and becoming less tolerant of dissent.
body: Official results show Hakainde Hichilema receiving roughly 60 percent of votes, compared with 38 percent for his main challenger, Brian Mundubile.
Zambia’s President Hakainde Hichilema has won re-election for a second term, according to the electoral commission, after a race marred by allegations of fraud.

Results released by the election commission in the early hours of Tuesday morning showed that Hichilema received roughly 60 percent of valid votes, compared with 38 percent for his main challenger, Brian Mundubile.
After a relatively quiet run-up to the August 13 vote, tensions escalated quickly.
On the night of the election, authorities arrested 11 people, including leading opposition figures, in a raid that involved an exchange of gunfire, while Mundubile was present.
The next day, the electoral commission suspended vote-counting for hours due to reports of violence against polling staff and the theft of ballot papers.
Mundubile said he had received information about the possible alteration of results forms from polling stations and called for an urgent independent investigation.
Hichilema’s camp said he was lying.

bullets.label: Next
bullets.text: It was Hichilema’s seventh run for the presidency, and he was widely expected to win due to the advantages of incumbency, while it was Mundubile’s first bid to become head of state.

stories.title: Trump's approval rating falls to 33%, lowest since inauguration — poll
stories.summary: WASHINGTON, August 18. US President Donald Trump's approval rating among Americans has fallen to 33%, its lowest level since his inauguration on January 20, 2025, according to a poll conducted jointly by Reuters and international polling firm Ipsos. Thirty-three percent of respondents approve of Trump's performance as president, while 64% disapprove. The remaining respondents did not answer. Eighty percent of those surveyed believe the US-Iran conflict will be prolonged, while 16% expect it to end within several weeks. According to polls regularly conducted by Reuters and Ipsos, the US president's approval rating had previously not fallen below 34% during his second term. It reached that level in June and April of this year. Trump's highest approval rating during his second term was recorded in January 2025, when 47% of respondents viewed his performance positively. During Trump's first presidential term, his approval rating fell to 33% in December 2017. The poll was conducted from August 14 to 17 among 1,166 U S adults.

stories.title: Huanggang Port points to the future of Greater Bay Area travel
stories.summary: The much-anticipated revamped Huanggang Port, expected to open later this year, should be seen as more than a story about faster clearance. Its deeper significance lies in a question that deserves wider discussion: if border functions can be redesigned, where should border control actually operate? Living in the Greater Bay Area, where people and businesses move across administrative boundaries every day, I have watched the meaning of borders change. A border is no longer simply a line...
